thread:
ops-bot: INCIDENT detected — inference-prod / us-east-1 reporting elevated 5xx errors and request timeouts. Severity: P1. Pager: @Sanjay (Oncall)

Sanjay (Oncall): I'm paged, looking now. swapping to console.

Sanjay (Oncall): quick signal check — error rate spike started ~2 mins ago, routes to model-x-quant have highest failures.

Alex (SRE): I can join — pulling logs, likely an autoscaler flapping or kernel OOM. Oncall, can you confirm any deploys in the last 10m?

Sanjay (Oncall): No deploys in last 30m. I see continuous 504 / 500 from worker nodes 12-14. CPU usage ok, GPU mem near capacity on node-13.

Alex (SRE): grabbing node-13 dmesg and docker logs. Adding temporary routing to fallback model variant to reduce load. Will post exact commands.

Alex (SRE): Action: applied routing rule to send 10% traffic to model-x-quant-lite and 90% to model-x-quant. Monitoring.

Maya (CS): Heads up — customers hitting production embeddings and chat might see failures. I will prepare a short customer note once we have impact scope.

Evelyn (PM): Need quick impact summary for leadership + status page copy. Keep it factual and short.

Alex (SRE): Root cause (initial): transient GPU memory pressure combined with a suboptimal batch size causing one worker to OOM and cascade with autoscaler churn. Mitigated by temporary routing + scale up.

Alex (SRE): Mitigation steps executed:
- reroute 10% traffic to model-x-quant-lite
- scaled worker pool in us-east-1 + drained node-13
- disabled continuous-batching for model-x-quant for now

Sanjay (Oncall): Observed error rate drop to baseline ~3m after mitigations. Keeping monitoring for 15m. Marking incident transitioning to recovery.

ops-bot: Status changed: INCIDENT -> RECOVERING. All hands stay on deck for now.

Maya (CS): Drafting status page update. Posting here for quick review.

Maya (CS): ```
Status: Partial service disruption — Resolved (recovering)
Start time: 2026-03-15T09:12:01Z
Summary: A subset of inference requests in us-east-1 experienced elevated errors and timeouts due to GPU memory pressure on a worker node. We mitigated the issue by redistributing traffic and scaling the worker pool.
Customer impact: Some requests to text-generation and embeddings may have failed or timed out for up to ~8 minutes.
Current status: Error rates returning to normal; continued monitoring.
Next steps: RCA in progress; we will follow up with customers with a summary and preventive actions.
```

Evelyn (PM): LGTM. Add link to customer follow-up once available.

Jules (Support): Customer FYI draft for affected tenants — pushing here so CS can quick-send after review.

Maya (CS): ```
Subject: Brief update on intermittent inference errors in us-east-1
Hi <CustomerName>,
We experienced intermittent failures for some inference requests between 09:12–09:20 UTC in us-east-1 affecting text-generation and embeddings. We routed traffic and scaled capacity; error rates have returned to normal.
We're investigating the root cause and will follow up with an RCA and preventive steps. Apologies for the disruption; let us know if you saw any downstream issues.
Regards,
Maya / Redwood Inference
```

Sanjay (Oncall): Timeline note for RCA:
- 09:11:45Z alert from latency detector
- 09:12:01Z pager fired
- 09:12:30Z mitigation: routing 10% -> model-x-quant-lite
- 09:14:10Z scaled pool + drained node-13
- 09:19:00Z error rates dropped to baseline
- 09:27:00Z monitoring stable, incident moved to recovering

Alex (SRE): For the RCA we should capture batching config, recent kernel upgrade on node-13, and model memory stats. Tentative cause: combination of slightly larger batch window in continuous-batching + a runaway KV cache size on node-13.

Maya (CS): Proposed customer-facing RCA summary (short):
- What happened: Brief GPU memory issue on a single worker caused elevated errors for a small fraction of requests in us-east-1.
- Impact: Some requests to generation/embeddings failed or timed out for up to ~8 minutes.
- Mitigation: We rerouted traffic, scaled capacity, and removed the offending worker.
- Prevention: We'll update batching controls, add an automated KV cache cap, and improve autoscaler cooldowns.

Evelyn (PM): Add commitment bullet: "We will provide follow-up with exact preventative changes within 72 hours."

Alex (SRE): Preventative actions list for internal + customer note:
- enforce KV cache size limit per-worker
- add dynamic batch-size cap when memory pressure detected
- tune autoscaler cooldowns to avoid churn cascades
- add alerting for per-worker GPU memory anomalies

Jules (Support): Queueing customer outreach for affected accounts: list pulled and DMing Maya with high-touch customers.

Maya (CS): Internal comms template (for ops and sales):
"Short incident summary + impact + mitigation + next steps". Example: "On 2026-03-15 at 09:12 UTC we observed transient GPU memory pressure in us-east-1 which caused elevated failures for a subset of inference requests. The team rerouted traffic and scaled capacity; service returned to normal by 09:19 UTC. An RCA is underway; preventions will be implemented and we will notify affected customers with details."

Sanjay (Oncall): Leaving a note for oncall rotation: if similar flapping happens, increase scale cap by +2 workers before routing changes.

Alex (SRE): I'll open the post-incident ticket with logs, batch config, and proposed fixes. ETA for changes: 48 hours for alerting + 72 hours for batching/kv changes.

Maya (CS): Sending customer email to low-touch cluster now; DMing Jules for enterprise list. Will attach the short RCA once Alex files the ticket.

ops-bot: Message recorded to incident channel and incident tracker updated: incident-2026-03-15-1767504321

Maya (CS): Thanks everyone. I'll post the finalized status page and customer follow-up after Alex's ticket is attached. :pray:
